text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bigger cabinet keeps veterans: Rock moves to Health, Eggleton touted for troubled Defence, McLellan takes Justice.
- Jessop admits false testimony: Police pressure led to change in story.
- Squeegee kids popping up all over: Police are cracking down on the wiper brigades but few teens fear the fines.
- Hague in position to win Tory post: Solid second in race to succeed Major.
- Ex-broker charged with fraud over clients' C$22-million loss: Forest Hill resident once seen as a superstar of Bay Street.
- Acid rain threat far from over: Suggested emission standards already out of date.
- Eaton's brass set for windfall: 20 ex-directors would share about C$8-million if court approves dividing pension surplus.
- CIBC unit sets price for Oppenheimer: Won't top C$400-million for U.S. brokerage.
- Reichmann returns to Mexico: Joins venture to build skyscraper stalled by peso crash.
- Financial markets counting on Martin to keep debt in line: Liberals can't afford to abandon deficit-cutting now, analysts say.
- Southam battle heats up: Hollinger says take it or leave it as two Canadian institutional investors line up with U.S. fund tycoon Michael Price, agreeing that C$23.50 is too low.
- Boliden issue expected to raise more than C$818 million.
